title: Capital Shift to Dhaka (Jahangirnagar)
subtitle: Islam Khan moves Bengal's Mughal capital from Rajmahal to Dhaka.
summary: In 1610, Islam Khan Chishti transferred the Mughal provincial capital of Bengal from Rajmahal to Dhaka and renamed it Jahangirnagar in official use. The move aligned administration with the Bhati frontier where major resistance networks operated.
heroTagline: Dhaka's rise as Jahangirnagar turned frontier warfare into capital governance.
whyItMatters: This event matters because it tied military strategy, river logistics, and governance to a new eastern center, enabling deeper Mughal consolidation.
longTermLegacy: Dhaka's elevation institutionalized a governance pattern in which eastern riverine control was central to Bengal's provincial management.
identityMemoryNotes: The 1610 shift is remembered as the moment Dhaka became the key Mughal command-and-administration node in Bengal's contested east.
